4. The plaintiff, afterwards, by way of an amendment dated 9-11-1992, sought the relief for recovery of khas possession of the upstairs (first floor) of the schedule property removing all the obstructions, hinderance and ousting the allottee from the said upstair. 

 37. Turning now to the contention raised from the side of the petitioner that the suit is not maintainable in view of the non-payment of ad valorem court-fee on the valuation of the suit. The petitioner in paragraph No. 2 of the application under Order XIV, rule 2 of the Code stated that the plaintiff did not file the required court-fee in view of seeking a decree of recovery of khas possession and for the non-payment of Court-fee, the suit is not maintainable. It is submitted from the side of the opposite party that the ad valorem Court-fee had been paid. This contention is supported from materials on record. On perusal of Order No. 37 dated 25-11-1992 it appears that Court-fee of Taka 2243.00 had been deposited in the court. The case of Shaukat Hossain and others vs. Abdul Hakim 42 DLR 508 is of no help to the petitioner.
